summary.text: Two mechanics argue over a cracked drive belt in a cramped, single-lamp garage; the older mechanic challenges first, and the younger mechanic answers without backing down.

description.text: In a cramped garage, a single bare work lamp hangs low and throws a hard pool of light over the open engine bay, leaving the back wall in a brown half-dark. The bay is crowded with hoses, oily fittings and a greasy engine block; a glazed, cracked drive belt sits exposed across the front pulley. The older mechanic, sleeves rolled to the elbow and hands dark with old grease, leans over the fender and jabs a finger at the split in the belt. He straightens, shoulders squared, and faces the younger mechanic across the engine. The younger mechanic keeps both hands on a wrench, his knuckles pale around the handle, and meets the older man's stare without stepping back. Metal tools rest in a tray, a rag hangs from the fender, and the cooling engine ticks faintly under the room tone. The older mechanic speaks his challenge in four terse words, jaw set; the younger man's expression hardens as he takes the point.
Low garage room tone and the faint tick of cooling metal.

The younger mechanic keeps both hands on a wrench and meets the older man's stare.
A wrench clinks against the fender, and the cooling engine ticks.
The camera holds a static shot.

On the far side of the engine bay, the younger mechanic stands in the tighter light of the work lamp, his face damp at the temple and his jaw working once before he answers. He wipes his palm on a rag, the cloth dragging over grease and skin, then lifts his chin and speaks his reply in four clipped words. The older mechanic's shoulder stays planted in the foreground, a dark wedge of coveralls and folded arm, unconvinced. Beyond them the garage wall is cluttered with hanging belts, a shelf of dented cans and a coiled air hose; the lamp sways a fraction and creaks, and the engine's cooling tick continues under the low room tone. The younger mechanic keeps his ground, the wrench still in his other hand, and the argument settles into a hard mutual stare.
